rationale: Origin is stated as synthetic generation from a knowledge graph plus encyclopedia text, and the generation method is described. No licence or terms and no consent or IRB statement appear (not required is not stated).

quotes.text: We randomly generated 5 distinct sets of test cases, each containing 300 unique patient cases

rationale: A sampling design is stated (random sampling of disease nodes, 5 sets of 300 cases), but there is no comparison of patient features with any named target population.

quotes.text: Conclusion and Safety: Diagnostic Correctness (DC) and Diagnostic Uncertainty (DU)

rationale: A safety-oriented rubric dimension (diagnostic uncertainty, overconfidence as a safety risk) is scored, which is the nearest thing to an unsafe-output test. No bias test of any kind is reported; the simulator-backbone sensitivity study is about ranking robustness, not bias. Weak evidence for 1.

quotes.text: This dynamic and knowledge-grounded sampling ensures that each case is coherent with domain expertise while being previously unseen

rationale: Dynamic case generation is a design control against contamination, but no measured overlap or memorization check is reported. The leakage review in 4.6 concerns diagnosis disclosure in dialogue, not training-data contamination.

quotes.text: This profile serves as the latent ground truth from which the patient agent simulates dialogue

rationale: The case profile is a latent ground truth held by the environment and the doctor agent acts on dialogue history, so isolation is implied by the design. The paper never states that the agent cannot reach the profile and names no mechanism.

searched: S1, S2, S3, S4, S5. Cases are generated dynamically at evaluation time and no released fixed case set is stated. The patient and examiner simulator (GPT-5) and the judge LLMs are live API models with no snapshot or date pinned, and no harness version is given.
searched: S1 (methods, experiments, appendix A1-A10), S2, S3, S4, S5. No oracle or scripted reference solution, nor any solvability check, is reported.

searched: S1 (Table 1, appendix tables), S2, S3, S4, S5. Only 15 real LLMs are reported; no do-nothing or random agent result.

rationale: The paper validates its own LLM judge against three human experts on 450 annotated cases with correlation figures. It also reports clinician validation of the patient and examiner agent outputs on 200 cases (99.0% no leakage, 93.5% realistic).

quotes.text: (mean \pm standard error) on ClinDEF

rationale: Standard errors accompany the headline scores. The resampling or variance unit (case, run, or case set) is not named, and clustering is not addressed.

quotes.text: conducted five independent runs for each model

rationale: Score-level variation over five runs per model is reported as standard error. No action-level or state-level agreement and no pass^k metric are reported; the runs may also use different case sets, so they are not strictly identical reruns.

quotes.text: Diag outputs o_{t}^{D}=d_{t} , representing the model’s final diagnostic decision that terminates the interaction.

rationale: A text-command protocol (Ask, Test, Diag) is defined and the environment response to each action is documented, including termination. No schema or enforced grammar, no read/write side-effect classification and no error returns are given. No S5 content in the packet, so S5 reach cannot be told.

quotes.text: the Patient Agent A_{P} and Examiner Agent A_{E} function as responsive environmental simulators

rationale: The paper discloses that patient and examiner responses are LLM simulated and checks their outputs with clinicians (leakage and fidelity on 200 cases), which is read as a conformance check. No S5 content in the packet, so reach of the disclosure to the agent cannot be shown.

quotes.text: Test results in o_{t}^{D}=r_{t} , denoting a request for an objective examination.
avoidance of under- or over-utilization

rationale: Test requests (orders) and the terminating Diag are identified, test results are simulated by an LLM examiner, and test over- and under-utilization is scored in the Test Justification dimension and via findings and turn metrics. Element (i) is borderline since the paper does not label actions as writes. S5 reach cannot be told.

quotes.text: To evaluate the more nuanced aspects of the diagnostic process, we employ an “LLM-as-a-Judge” paradigm

rationale: Grader input is named (LLM judge over the dialogue; final diagnosis for accuracy) with a rationale (nuanced process aspects). Validation is by correlation with human experts on 450 cases and gives no per-class error rates on labelled correct and incorrect outcomes, so element (iii) is not met.

quotes.text: Reviewers found that 99.0% of cases contained no such information leakage.

rationale: Answer leakage through the patient and examiner agents is checked by clinicians on 200 cases. There is no held-out or private split (cases are generated dynamically) and no canary or provenance marker.
